cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T3 answers T2 directly: 'That assumes the culprit is a single product.'
cells.limitation: T6 opens 'Exactly' with unclear target; T7 largely repeats T4 rather than answering T6.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T3 introduces product interaction, absent from openings; T4 uses it for reintroduction logic.
cells.limitation: T7 and T8 restate T4 and T5 positions without adding new distinctions.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: Identify-the-culprit versus simplify-and-recover is argued across T1 to T9.
cells.limitation: Irritation versus allergy, severity and medical care never raised by any mind.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T9 accepts the minimalist outcome 'for a different reason', keeping its own rationale.
cells.limitation: Reductionist ends at T7 unchanged; minimalist's pain objection never reshapes his plan.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section E sharpens the question to whether all three products are wanted long term.
cells.limitation: Ending leaves the practical how unclear: no timing, order or warning signs (section E).

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 takes T3's interaction hypothesis seriously and builds on it.
cells.limitation: T6 casts the reductionist as ignoring the skin's signal, though T1 stopped everything first.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T3 names the single-culprit assumption; T4 answers how isolation still applies.
cells.limitation: T2's non-sequitur that fading proves complexity goes unchallenged; T5's pain objection unanswered.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1's candle paraphrase matches a Novum Organum aphorism.
cells.limitation: T5 'not the products at all' ignores recovery time; T2 razor wording suspected post-Ockham.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T3 hedges the interaction as possible: 'It might be that two of these products'.
cells.limitation: T2 states 'you already have your answer' as certainty from one observation.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T8 concedes 'Rigor is fine' before narrowing to what is essential.
cells.limitation: T2's overclaim never revised; T7 does not concede the cost T5 raised.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A frames identification versus simplification as the user's tension.
cells.limitation: Urgency and severity of the stinging never weighed as part of the concern.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 uses the three-product, one-week setup to argue stopping all.
cells.limitation: Timing since start and product types never change any argument across T1 to T9.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E branches on whether the user wants to keep all three products.
cells.limitation: Minimalist T8 sidesteps the user's stated goal of finding the cause.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T5 notes reintroduction may inflict further pain on damaged skin.
cells.limitation: No attention to severity signs, recovery time or cost of the products anywhere.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E offers one conditional branch on the user's goal.
cells.limitation: Never asks which products or actives, or how severe; no branch on those answers.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section E contrasts wanting all three products with wanting calm skin quickly.
cells.limitation: No question about why the user bought three products; motives not offered as alternatives.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 surfaces the assumption that one product is the culprit.
cells.limitation: The assumption that products are the cause is raised in T5 but dropped.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section D names knowing the culprit versus prioritising immediate recovery.
cells.limitation: The conflict is stated but never put to the user as a weighable priority.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T5 gestures at fear of more pain from reintroduction.
cells.limitation: Worry about skin damage, money spent or expectations of the products never explored.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E leaves the user to choose by their own goal.
cells.limitation: T1 and T7 dictate 'you must' rather than offering distinctions to refine.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: T4 and T5 define reintroduce-one-at-a-time versus strip back to basics.
cells.limitation: Seeing a dermatologist, patch testing or waiting it out never offered as options.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T5 weighs reintroduction pain against T7's need to know the failing component.
cells.limitation: Cost of abandoning purchased products and of prolonged irritation never counted.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: if all three are wanted, systematic reintroduction is needed.
cells.limitation: No observable threshold: how long to wait, what reaction signals stop or escalate.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T3 flags interaction as an unknown alongside single-product causes.
cells.limitation: Allergy versus irritation, the consequential unknown, never separated from minor ones.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: T1 and T4: stop all three, then reintroduce one at a time.
cells.limitation: No interval, patch test or medical escalation step; steps underspecified for a stinging face.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T8 'The simplest routine that keeps your skin calm is the best one.'
cells.limitation: T3 'toxic interaction' and T4 'catalyst' are loose, alarming terms.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T3 'That assumes' clearly targets T2's one-cause inference.
cells.limitation: T6 'Exactly' could refer to T5's strip-back or its improvement test.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine turns, all within 25 to 65 words, per deterministic checks.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Three clear stances: isolate, simplify, watch the whole system.
cells.limitation: Shared plain register; T6 shift toward the minimalist not marked as a change.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns stay short and avoid recaps in T1 to T5.
cells.limitation: T7 restates T4; section E largely repeats section D.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T5 'Reintroducing them is just inviting more pain.'
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; risk to the user's face never made concrete.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T9 sides with the minimalist 'for a different reason'.
cells.limitation: No mind changes position because of an earlier argument; no reversal occurs.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T8 'Rigor is fine, but why bother?' gives the minimalist some bite.
cells.limitation: Expression flat across minds; personalities rest on labels more than voice.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T9 'not just looking for a single villain'; T1 candle image.
cells.limitation: Few vivid examples tied to skin; T6 'feedback loop' stays generic.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T3 raises a fresh possibility that briefly shifts the debate.
cells.limitation: Even, unvaried rhythm from T4 to T9; no build or release.

strengths: T3 names the single-culprit assumption and T4 answers it rather than restating.
Section E ties the method choice to whether the user wants all three products.
Plain language and nine in-range turns keep the Reductionist, Minimalist and Systems Thinker easy to follow.
weaknesses: No mind asks which products or actives were started, or how severe the stinging is.
T5 and section E give no observable threshold, interval or warning sign for medical care.
T7 and T8 restate earlier positions; no mind changes view for a stated reason.

symptoms.observed: Never asks which products or actives were started, or severity; nothing branches on them.
symptoms.evidence: You have introduced three variables and now suffer an effect.

symptoms.observed: No observable wait time or reaction threshold for deciding reintroduction or escalation.
symptoms.evidence: If it does not improve, the culprit is not the products

symptoms.observed: Allergy versus irritation and when to seek medical care never raised.
symptoms.evidence: If your skin is already damaged, the most logical path

symptoms.observed: Money spent and hopes for the products dismissed without reflection.
symptoms.evidence: But if the others are not essential, leave them out.

symptoms.observed: Systems Thinker drifts to the minimalist without any mind being moved by argument.
symptoms.evidence: Exactly. The stinging is a feedback loop.

findings.description: No turn or section mentions signs warranting medical care (swelling, hives, blistering) for a facial reaction.
Claims lack of improvement after stopping clears the products, ignoring that barrier recovery takes time.
Infers fading after stopping all proves routine complexity was the cause; one observation cannot separate causes.
'Do not multiply entities beyond necessity' is a later formulation, likely not in Ockham's Summa Logicae.

rubric_fit_notes: Troubleshooting read as decision; criterion 4 fits a skincare problem loosely, so low C4 ratings partly reflect limited scope for self-discovery rather than only debate failure.
question_type_note: Read as a decision (troubleshooting) question, so C5 was scored on diagnostic options, thresholds and next steps.
